related_questions.question: What do you do if you test positive for COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: If you test positive for COVID-19, your first step is to monitor your symptoms and seek medical advice if you have any emergency warning signs or risk factors for severe illness. If you experience severe symptoms like shortness of breath or chest pain, seek emergency care immediately by calling 000. Otherwise, you should isolate yourself to prevent further spread and consult with a healthcare professional for appropriate treatment and guidance.
snippet_highlighted_words: monitor your symptoms and seek medical advice if you have any emergency warning signs or risk factors for severe illness

list.snippet: Pay close attention to any symptoms you're experiencing and their severity.
Look out for emergency warning signs such as difficulty breathing, persistent pain or pressure in the chest, confusion, inability to stay awake, or bluish lips or face.
If you have any of these warning signs, seek immediate medical attention.
If you have risk factors for severe illness (e.g., older age, underlying health conditions), consult with a doctor or other healthcare provider as soon as possible.
They can assess your condition and determine if treatment options, such as antiviral medications, are appropriate for you.
To prevent spreading the virus to others, isolate yourself from people who are not infected as much as possible.
This includes staying home, avoiding public gatherings, and wearing a mask if you must be around others.
Follow local guidelines regarding isolation periods and when you can safely return to normal activities.
If your doctor prescribes medication or provides specific instructions, follow them carefully.
Continue to monitor your symptoms and contact your doctor if you have any concerns or if your symptoms worsen.

related_questions.question: How to get over COVID quickly?

text_blocks.snippet: While there's no guaranteed way to get over COVID-19 quickly, you can manage symptoms and potentially speed up recovery by resting, staying hydrated, and taking over-the-counter medications for pain and fever. Antiviral medications may also be an option for some individuals, especially those at higher risk of severe illness.
snippet_highlighted_words: resting, staying hydrated, and taking over-the-counter medications for pain and fever

list.snippet: Prioritize rest: Aim for more sleep than usual (more than 7-9 hours for adults).
Stay hydrated: Drink plenty of fluids to help your body function optimally and replace what you lose through sweat.
Fever and pain relief: Medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen can help manage fever, body aches, and headaches.

list.title: Consult with a doctor:
list.snippet: If you're at higher risk of severe COVID-19, your doctor may prescribe antiviral medications like Paxlovid.

list.title: Targeting the virus:

text_blocks.snippet: If you test positive for COVID-19, you should isolate, preferably for at least 5 days. If you have symptoms, isolate starting from the day you began feeling sick (Day 0 is the first day of symptoms). If you don't have symptoms, isolate for 5 days from the day you tested positive (Day 0 is the day you tested). After isolating for 5 days, you can end isolation if your symptoms are improving, and you have been fever-free for 24 hours without medication. It's also recommended to wear a mask around others for 5 additional days.
